transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I guess... what brings me in is I hardly eat right anymore. Some days it's just coffee and maybe a piece of bread. My pants are hanging loose on me, which is funny because I used to buy my jeans at this little shop downtown, right next to the hardware store where my buddy Mike used to work. Mike was always fixing up those old muscle cars, you know? He had this '69 Chevelle that was just... man, it was beautiful. Cherry red. We used to drive it down to the lake on weekends. The lake gets so crowded now, though, not like when we were kids. People just leave their trash everywhere... but yeah, I don't really have an appetite lately.
Have you been feeling sad or down lately?

Yeah, I guess so. Most days I wake up with this heavy, empty feeling right here in my chest. It's like... like nothing good is waiting for me anyway, so I just want to keep my head down. Keep my head down and not look at anything. I just lay there and stare at the wall. 

The paint is actually peeling by the window right now. I was supposed to fix it, get some of that spackle stuff from the hardware store. The one where Mike worked, like I was saying before. They sell these little buckets of it, but you gotta make sure you get the right metal trowel. If you use a cheap plastic one, it snaps right in half. I broke two of them trying to patch a hole at my old apartment. The landlord was so mad, he threatened to keep my whole deposit over a tiny hole. Can you believe that? Over a hole the size of a dime. He was a real cheapskate, that guy. He drove this beat-up old station wagon that smelled like wet dog... but yeah, I just get that heavy feeling a lot.
How much weight would you say you've lost since you first noticed your appetite changed?

I don't know exactly... I haven't stepped on a scale in a long time. I just know my belt is on the last notch, and it's still sliding down. I had to punch a new hole in it with an awl. You know, an awl? It's like an ice pick but for leather. I got it at a garage sale a few years back. This old guy was selling all his woodworking tools because he was moving into one of those assisted living places. He had some really nice chisels, too. I should have bought the chisels, but I didn't have the cash on me. Cash is king at garage sales, you know? If you show up with a twenty-dollar bill, people will just give you a whole box of stuff just to get rid of it. I got a whole box of old cassette tapes once for five bucks. Mostly classic rock... but yeah, I don't know how many pounds it's been. Just a lot, I guess.
Do you still enjoy activities that you used to find pleasurable?

Not really... no. I used to like walking by the lake, you know? And working on my little model kits. I had these World War II planes I was putting together. You gotta use this special cement glue for them, though, and it smells real strong. It comes in this little metal tube, and if you squeeze it too hard, it gets all over your fingers and dries like glass. You almost have to peel your skin off to get it off. 

My uncle used to build them all the time. He had a whole fleet of them hanging from his ceiling on fishing line. He was actually the one who taught me how to tie a proper knot for fishing. We'd go down to the creek and catch these huge catfish. Some people won't eat catfish because they say they're bottom feeders, just eating mud and whatever sinks, but if you coat them in cornmeal and fry them up in a cast-iron skillet... man, there's nothing better. Cast iron is the only way to cook fish. You can't wash the pan with soap, though, or it ruins the seasoning. You just gotta wipe it out with a paper towel and some coarse salt. My grandma had a skillet that was probably a hundred years old, weighed a ton... 

But anyway, yeah. The model kits. Now they just sit there on my desk. I just look at them and it's like... like they belong to somebody else. I just don't care about them anymore.
Do you often feel nervous or anxious?

I don't know if I'd call it nervous... maybe sometimes. Mostly I just feel tired. But my neighbor, Mrs. Gable, she's always nervous. She's got this little yappy dog, a Pomeranian I think, and it barks at every single leaf that blows past her porch. She's always looking out through her blinds, pulling them down just a tiny crack. Those plastic blinds, you know? They always get tangled up if you pull the string wrong. 

I tried to fix a set of those for her once, but the little plastic gear inside the top rail was completely stripped. You can't even buy those replacement parts at the hardware store anymore. You have to order them online, and by the time you pay shipping, you might as well just buy a whole new set of blinds. I told her that, but she didn't want to spend the money. She's on a fixed income, she said. Her husband worked at the auto plant for thirty years before they shut it down in the nineties. 

He had a really nice collection of vintage hubcaps in his garage. Ford, Chevy, even some old Studebaker ones. I don't know what happened to them after he passed. Probably went to the scrapyard. Scrapyards don't even pay good money for steel anymore, mostly just copper and aluminum. People will steal the copper pipes right out from under a vacant house just to make a quick buck... but no, I wouldn't say I feel anxious. Just heavy, like I said.
Do you often feel guilty about anything?

Yeah, I do. All the time, really. I just keep thinking I'm no good, you know? Ever since I lost that job, my relatives have had to help me out with money and groceries. My sister brought over a whole casserole last week. Tuna noodle, with the crushed up potato chips on top. You gotta use the plain chips, though, the ruffled ones get too soggy when you bake it. 

She brought it over in one of those Pyrex dishes with the blue flowers on the side. The vintage ones. Those things are actually worth a lot of money now if you look on eBay. People collect them. I don't know why you'd want to collect baking dishes, but people collect everything. I knew a guy who collected old glass insulators from telephone poles. He had hundreds of them lined up on shelves in his basement. Green ones, clear ones, some really rare blue ones. He'd go walking along abandoned railroad tracks just looking for them in the weeds. You gotta watch out for copperheads if you do that, though. They blend right in with the dead leaves. My cousin got bit by a copperhead once when he was stacking firewood. His leg swelled up like a balloon, had to go to the ER and get anti-venom. Anti-venom is crazy expensive, like thousands of dollars a vial. 

But yeah, I just sit here and replay every single mistake I made at that job, like I just ruined everything for myself. I feel terrible that my family has to carry my weight.
Do you often feel like you're worthless?

Yeah... worthless. That's exactly it. I just keep thinking I'm no good for anything anymore. Especially since I lost that job. I was running the forklift in the warehouse, the big propane ones, not the electric ones. You gotta change out those propane tanks when they get low, and they're heavy, man. You have to wear those thick leather gloves so you don't freeze your hands off if the valve leaks. Propane gets freezing cold when it decompresses. 

My buddy Dale, he tried to deep-fry a turkey once for Thanksgiving using a propane burner, and he didn't thaw the bird all the way. You ever see what happens when you drop a frozen turkey into boiling peanut oil? It basically explodes. The oil boils over, hits the flame, and whoosh. Caught his whole wooden deck on fire. They had to get the fire department out there and everything. Those fire trucks are so loud when they come down the street, shaking the windows. The dalmatian dogs they used to have on fire trucks, you know, they actually used those to keep the horses calm back when they pulled the water wagons. Dalmatians are high-energy dogs, though, they need a lot of running space or they get destructive. 

But yeah... I just sit around now and replay every little mistake I made at that warehouse, like I just ruined everything. And now my relatives are the ones paying for my groceries and helping me out. It just makes me feel completely useless.
Have you ever thought about harming yourself?

No, I don't think about that. I mean, I feel bad, but I wouldn't do anything like that. My uncle, though, he had this old hunting rifle he kept up in the attic. A Winchester, I think, lever-action. You know those old cowboy movies where they spin the gun around by the lever to cock it? You can't actually do that in real life, it'll break your fingers or jam the mechanism. 

Anyway, he kept it in this canvas case that smelled like mothballs and gun oil. Gun oil has this really specific smell, kind of sweet but chemical. People use Hoppe's No. 9, that's the classic one. My buddy used to use it to clean his dirt bike chain, which is completely the wrong thing to use. You need a proper chain lube or the O-rings dry out. Dirt bikes are dangerous anyway. I saw a guy at the track once hit a whoop section too fast, went right over the handlebars. Broke his collarbone in three places. Collarbones are the easiest bone in the body to break, they say. It's like a built-in shock absorber for your neck. But no... I don't want to hurt myself. I just feel so heavy all the time.
Are there any activities that you still enjoy doing?

Not really. I used to like walking by the lake, you know, just taking it easy. And working on my little model kits. I had all these World War II airplanes, the P-51 Mustangs and the B-17 bombers. You gotta get the decals just right on those, using that micro-sol stuff so they melt into the panel lines. Otherwise they look like cheap stickers. 

My cousin tried to build a model ship once, the Titanic. He used superglue instead of model cement and got it all over his fingers. Superglue was actually invented during the Vietnam War to close up wounds fast on the battlefield. They'd just spray it right on the cut to stop the bleeding. Medical grade, though, not the stuff you buy at the hardware store. Hardware store glue will give you a chemical burn if you get too much of it on your skin. I got a burn once from touching a hot muffler on a lawnmower. Those Briggs & Stratton engines get blazing hot. You gotta let them cool down for like an hour before you check the oil or you'll fry your hand. 

But yeah, I don't do any of that anymore. The models just sit there on the desk now. I look at them and it's like... I don't know, like they belong to somebody else. I just don't have the energy for it.
Are there any small things that still bring you some joy or pleasure?

No, not really. I mean, like I was saying, I used to really like going down by the lake. Just walking, looking at the water. The water gets this weird green color in August, though, from the algae blooms. You know about that? It's from all the fertilizer runoff from the farms up north. The nitrogen gets into the water and the algae just goes crazy. It chokes out all the fish because it uses up all the oxygen in the water. 

My buddy caught a catfish out of there once that was almost three feet long. Catfish are bottom feeders, they'll eat anything. He said he found a whole spark plug in its stomach when he cleaned it. Spark plugs are a pain to change on those newer cars, they put them way in the back against the firewall so you can't reach them without taking off the whole intake manifold. You drop a socket wrench down in there, it's gone forever. You gotta get one of those telescoping magnets to fish it out. Magnets are crazy, though, how they work. The Earth is basically just one giant magnet because of the iron core spinning around. That's why compasses work. 

But no, I don't get any joy out of things anymore. Even my model planes... they're just sitting there. I look at them and it's just... nothing. Like somebody else built them. I just don't care about any of it now.
How long have you been feeling this heavy, empty feeling?

Well, let's see... this depressed spell has been hanging over me for about five months now. Yeah, five months. That would put it back around October, right when all the leaves start falling. 

I hate dealing with leaves. The guy next door has this massive oak tree, and every year it just dumps everything right onto my property. Oak is incredibly hard wood, though. They use it to make whiskey barrels. You know they have to actually set the inside of the barrel on fire to char it? That's what gives the whiskey that smoky flavor. The charcoal acts like a filter. Charcoal is really just wood that gets baked in an oven without any oxygen. My buddy tried making his own lump charcoal once in a metal 55-gallon drum and almost burned his whole garage down. Garages are a pain to rebuild, especially with how much lumber costs now. A single sheet of plywood is ridiculously expensive. Plywood is actually pretty genius, though, it's just thin layers of wood glued together with the grain crisscrossing so it doesn't snap. You gotta use a carbide-tipped saw blade to cut it, though, or it splinters like crazy. Carbide is tough stuff, they put it on drill bits to chew right through solid concrete. Concrete is weird because it doesn't actually dry out, it cures through this whole chemical reaction. It takes like almost a whole month to reach its full strength... 

But, um... yeah. About five months. That's how long it's been hanging over me. Just a solid five months of feeling empty.
Are there any activities that you used to enjoy but no longer find pleasure in?

Well, like I was saying before, the models. The model planes. I used to really get into them, you know? And the lake, taking walks down there. But now... I don't know, it's just gone. The models are just sitting on my desk collecting dust. I look at them and it's like somebody else made them, not me. Dust is actually mostly dead skin cells, which is pretty gross if you think about it. Your body is just constantly shedding skin all the time. That's why mattresses get so heavy after a few years, they just fill up with dust mites eating all that dead skin. Dust mites are microscopic, you can't even see them, but they're everywhere. They look like little aliens under a microscope. Speaking of aliens, I watched this documentary the other night about the Voyager golden record. They sent this gold-plated record out into space in the 70s with sounds of Earth on it, just in case aliens ever find it. Gold is the best metal for that because it never rusts or tarnishes. It doesn't react with oxygen. That's why they use it in electronics, like on the little pins inside a computer processor. Computers get so hot, though. You have to have thermal paste between the chip and the fan or it'll just melt itself in seconds. 

But yeah... the models and the lake. I just don't care about them anymore. They just sit there.
Are there any activities that you still find pleasure in?

No, I really don't think there's anything left. Like I told you, I used to like walking by the lake and working on my little model kits. But now they just sit there, and I look at them like they belong to somebody else. 

It's funny how glue works on those models, though. You have to use this special plastic cement. It doesn't actually stick the pieces together, it literally melts the plastic so the two pieces fuse into one solid piece. It's basically chemical welding. Welding is crazy dangerous if you don't know what you're doing. You can literally go blind if you look at the arc without a helmet. It burns your corneas. My uncle used to weld pipes for the oil rigs down in the Gulf. Those guys make insane money, but they're out on the water for weeks at a time. The ocean is just terrifying when you really think about it. We know more about the surface of the moon than we do about the bottom of the ocean. There's trenches down there so deep that if you dropped Mount Everest into them, the peak would still be a mile underwater. The pressure down there is so intense it would crush a submarine like a soda can. Soda cans are made of aluminum now, but they used to be made of tin. Tin rusts, though. Aluminum doesn't rust, it just oxidizes on the surface and that protects the rest of the metal. 

But no, I don't get any pleasure out of anything anymore. Not the lake, not the models, nothing.
Are there any activities that you still find pleasure in or look forward to?

I really don't. I mean, I know I already said it, but it's just the truth. I used to really like going down by the lake, just walking around, and putting together those little model kits. But now... they just sit there on my desk. I just stare at them and it's like they belong to some other guy. 

It's weird how things just stop mattering. Like time just stops. Time is a crazy concept anyway. Did you know that time actually moves slower if you're going faster? It's called time dilation. Einstein figured it out. Like, if you were in a spaceship going close to the speed of light, you'd age slower than people back on Earth. The speed of light is the absolute speed limit of the universe. Nothing can go faster than 186,000 miles per second. Light from the sun takes about eight minutes to reach us. So if the sun exploded right now, we wouldn't even know it for eight minutes. We'd just be sitting here, totally clueless. The sun is just a giant ball of hydrogen fusing into helium. Helium is what they put in balloons, obviously, but we're actually running out of it on Earth. It's used in MRI machines to keep the magnets super cold. Magnets are fascinating. The Earth itself is a giant magnet, which is why compasses work. The magnetic field protects us from solar wind, which would otherwise strip away our atmosphere. Mars lost its magnetic field a long time ago, and that's why it's a dead planet now. They want to send people to Mars, but I don't know why anyone would want to live in a freezing desert where you can't even breathe the air. 

But yeah... I don't look forward to anything. The lake, the models... it's all just nothing to me now.
Are there any small things that you still find pleasure in?

Doc, I swear I'm not trying to be difficult, but I feel like a broken record here. Like I keep saying, no. Not even the small stuff. I told you about the lake and the models. I used to love just going down there, or sitting at my desk with those little kits, but now... I just look at them and feel absolutely nothing. Like they're some stranger's junk just taking up space. 

I used to watch the ducks down at the lake, too. People always throw bread at them, but you're really not supposed to do that. It's super bad for them. It gives them this thing called angel wing where their feathers grow out all twisted because bread is just empty carbs. Carbs turn straight into sugar in your body. Sugar is actually way more addictive than people think. I saw this video where they said it lights up your brain exactly like cocaine does. Cocaine is just a plant, though. It comes from those leaves down in the jungle in South America. They used to actually put it in soda back in the day, which is wild to think about. Now they just pump everything full of caffeine. Caffeine is actually a natural bug repellent. Plants make it to paralyze insects that try to chew on their leaves. So every time people drink coffee, they're basically drinking bug spray. Bugs outnumber us by like a billion to one, you know. If they ever decided to organize and attack, we wouldn't stand a chance. Ants can carry like fifty times their own body weight. If a guy could do that, he could pick up a whole truck. Trucks are getting too complicated now, though. Everything is run by computers, so if one little sensor breaks, the whole engine just shuts down. You can't even fix your own vehicle anymore without plugging it into a laptop. 

But yeah... I don't know what else to tell you, man. Small things, big things... I just don't care about the models or the lake or any of it anymore.
Are there any activities that you still find pleasure in or enjoy doing?

Look, I don't know how many different ways I can answer the exact same thing, doc. We just went over this. No. Nothing. Zero. I used to go down to the lake, I used to do my model kits, but now... I look at the boxes sitting there and it's like they're not even mine. It's just dead plastic. 

Plastic is ruining the whole planet anyway, you know? It takes like a thousand years to break down. I saw on TV there's this giant island of garbage floating out in the Pacific Ocean that's twice the size of Texas. Texas is massive. They even have their own power grid down there, which is why the whole state shut down that one time it got freezing cold. People were literally freezing inside their own houses. You'd think a place with all that oil money would have better wires and stuff. Oil is literally just dead dinosaurs, which is pretty crazy if you think about it. We're driving around using T-Rex juice. Dinosaurs were around for millions of years and then one big rock from space just wiped them completely out. Asteroids are basically just giant space bullets. If one of them heads for us today, we're toast. In the movies they always blow them up with nukes, but real life doesn't work like that. If you blow it up, it just turns into a million smaller rocks on fire raining down on everyone. Fire is weird, it's not even a solid or a gas, it's like... plasma or something. 

But yeah. No. I don't enjoy the models. I don't enjoy the lake. I don't enjoy anything at all. Just like I keep telling you.
Is there anything at all that you still find gives you pleasure or enjoyment?

Doc... come on. Are you messing with me? I feel like I'm losing my mind here. We've been over this like four times now. No. There is nothing. Nothing gives me pleasure. Nothing gives me enjoyment. 

Like I said, I used to really like going for walks down by the lake, or sitting at my desk putting those little model kits together. But now? I just look at them and it's like they belong to somebody else entirely. Just useless pieces of plastic. 

It's funny how things are put together, though. Like, models have all those tiny little parts you have to glue. Glue is actually a crazy invention if you think about it. The Romans used to make glue out of boiled animal hides and hooves. They built an entire empire using animal parts and concrete. Roman concrete actually gets stronger over time because they mixed volcanic ash into it. Volcanoes are terrifying. There's a supervolcano under Yellowstone right now, and if it blows, it'll cover half the country in ash. Ash is basically just tiny shards of glass, so if you breathe it in, it shreds your lungs from the inside out. Lungs are weird organs. They're the only organ that can float on water. If you drop a lung in a bucket, it just bobs there like an apple. Apple picking used to be a big thing around here in the fall, but all the orchards keep getting bought up by developers. They just tear down all the trees and build these massive, ugly subdivisions where all the houses look exactly the same. They use the cheapest materials possible, too. Half those houses will probably blow over in a strong wind. 

But... yeah. I don't know what else to say. The lake, the models... I don't care about any of it. Nothing gives me enjoyment. I really hope we don't have to go over this again, doc.
Is there anything that you look forward to or that brings you a sense of excitement or joy?

Are you actually kidding me right now, doc? Is this a joke? Is there a hidden camera in here? Because I swear I just answered this exact same question four times in a row. 

No. There is no excitement. There is no joy. Like I have been saying since I sat down in this chair... I used to like walking by the lake. I used to like working on my little model kits. But now they just sit there on the desk gathering dust, and I look at them like they belong to somebody else entirely. 

Speaking of dust, did you know that like eighty percent of the dust in your house is actually just dead human skin? It's really gross if you think about it. We're just constantly shedding pieces of ourselves everywhere we go. Snakes do that too, but they do it all at once. They just peel out of their old skin like a dirty sock. I watched this show about snakes in Australia once. Basically every animal in Australia is designed to kill you. They have this one thing, the box jellyfish, and if it stings you, your heart just stops beating in like three minutes. The ocean is completely terrifying, honestly. They say we know more about the surface of the moon than we do about the bottom of our own ocean. Which makes no sense because the moon is thousands of miles away in space. They say the moon controls the ocean tides because of gravity, but nobody actually knows what gravity even *is*. It's just a theory. Like, if gravity just suddenly turned off for one single second, we'd all go flying up into the sky at a thousand miles an hour because the earth is spinning so fast. Spinning makes you dizzy because of the liquid inside your ears. Ears are weird because they never stop growing. When you're an old man, your ears and your nose are just gonna be huge. 

But look, man... I don't know what you want me to say. I don't look forward to anything. Not the lake, not the models, nothing. Can we please, please move on to a different question now?
